notes:
Everything since 1.24, including a fix for the screen jolting as you work.

**Tapping a mark no longer moves it.** Tapping a piston, a link or a pedal stamp to edit it would nudge it slightly out of place, so it then had to be dragged back. The app was treating almost any tap as a very short drag. It now waits to see whether you are really dragging before moving anything, on every mark tool.

**The screen no longer jolts as you tap.** The whole page would jump down and back on roughly every other tap. This was previously put down to the display's refresh mode; it was not, and it is now fixed properly.

**Every kind of link is on one menu.** Place a link and you are asked what it should do: go to a page in this piece, go to a page in another piece, make a two-way link, or make a back button. The long-press on the Link tool is gone, so nothing is hidden. You can also change what an existing link does instead of deleting it and starting again.

This also fixes the second tablet getting stuck placing back buttons until the app was restarted.

**Favourite pieces are pinned to the top when choosing a link target.** Tap the star next to any piece. Favourites sync between tablets.

**Scrolling the piece list no longer picks a piece by accident** when you let go with your finger.

**Links always take you where they say.** A link into a piece whose first page is hidden would quietly ignore the page it named and take you back to wherever you last were in that piece instead.

**Writing in performance mode is now two settings, and better named.** In Sidebar Settings: "Write with the pen without leaving performance mode", and under it "…and enter edit mode once you stop writing". Turn the second one off and the pen still writes, but you stay in performance mode afterwards, so edge taps keep turning pages. Both on is what the old single setting did, and that is what you already have.

**Filter and sort your library by composer, difficulty and the rest**, alongside the existing tags.

**Collections list the pieces inside them**, and you can jump straight into one from the page you are on.

**Each piece in a setlist carries its own settings.**

**Edit any of a piece's details on the tablet**, rather than only on the computer.

**Hymn indexes are shared with the computer** along with everything else.

Your library, annotations and licence are not affected.
